faq.q: What is the life cycle of a plant?
faq.a: A flowering plant goes round a cycle: seed, seedling, grown plant, flower, pollination, then fruit with new seeds, which grow into new plants.
asks: What are the stages of a plant's life?

faq.a: Pollination is when pollen moves from the male part of a flower to the female part, usually of another flower. Bees, butterflies, birds, bats and the wind carry pollen.
A fruit grows from the flower to protect the seeds and help them travel. Animals eat tasty fruit and drop the seeds somewhere new.
Yes! To a scientist, a fruit is the part that grows from a flower and holds seeds, so tomatoes, cucumbers, chillies and pumpkins are fruits.
No. Ferns and mosses make tiny spores instead of seeds, and pine trees make seeds in cones. But most plants we see, from grass to mango trees, are flowering plants.

facts: Scientifically, a fruit is the ripened ovary of a flower that contains seeds.
A large sunflower head can contain more than 1000 seeds.

quiz.say: What carries pollen from one flower to another?
quiz.why: Bees, and other insects, birds and the wind, carry pollen between flowers.

wrong.1: Roots stay underground and drink water.
wrong.2: Rain clouds do not carry pollen; wind sometimes does.

quiz.say: What does a flower turn into after pollination?
quiz.why: After pollination, the flower grows into a fruit that holds the new seeds.

wrong.0: Roots come from seeds, not from flowers.
wrong.2: Leaves grow on the stem, not from flowers.
